SOURCE: banner library, copper-peptide-day-repair-cream--D-face-full-eyes-open-right gpt_image_01 (2048x848, 2.42:1). Label checked at 100%: Skingenetix / COPPER PEPTIDE / ADVANCED DAY REPAIR / PREMIUM FORMULA, correct.

CANVAS EXTENDED, NOT CROPPED. The banner box is 100vw x 440px, so its aspect follows the viewport - 3.27:1 at 1440, 3.44:1 at 1512, 4.36:1 at 1920 - and a 2.42:1 frame is narrower than all of them, so object-fit cover was cropping the height. Extended leftward to 3750x848 (4.42:1), just past the widest of those, so the full height survives every common desktop width. object-position is right center, so surplus width is always cropped off the extension, never off the model or the jar.

THIS FRAME IS THE HARD CASE, AND THE SERUM ONE WAS NOT. Her ARM touches the left edge: the leftmost columns read backdrop at mean 16 down to row 739, then jump to mean 87-141. So it takes the pdrn shoulder treatment, but with numbers measured off THIS photograph rather than pdrn's: its arm runs y=742 at x=0 to y=601 at x=290, i.e. 0.48px down per px left, against pdrn's 0.62.

ONE FAULT WORTH RECORDING. The first build printed two dark lens-shaped ghosts across the extension. Cause was the texture box: (0,650,0,600) looks like backdrop and is not - it clips her shoulder, max luminance 174 against a backdrop of ~16 - and mirror-tiling that across 1702px repeated the shoulder edge twice. The subject first intrudes into cols 0-700 at row ~550, so the box now stops at row 400, verified max 23. Measured, not eyeballed, is the whole difference.
